description: An introduction to da'wah, the duty of inviting people to Islam and to good, covering its meaning, importance, Qur'anic methods, the qualities of a good caller, the example of the Prophet (PBUH), and its etiquette and challenges in the modern world.

mcq.questionText: What is the literal meaning of the Arabic word 'da'wah'?
mcq.explanation: Da'wah comes from the Arabic root meaning to call, invite or summon. In Islam it refers to inviting people to Islam and to all that is good.

mcq.questionText: Which Qur'anic verse outlines the three main methods of da'wah: wisdom, good preaching and arguing in the best manner?
mcq.explanation: Surah An-Nahl 16:125 instructs the believer to invite to the way of the Lord with wisdom (hikmah), good instruction (maw'izah hasanah) and to argue in the best manner.

mcq.questionText: The Arabic term 'hikmah' used in the methods of da'wah means:
mcq.explanation: Hikmah means wisdom: presenting Islam in the right way, at the right time, to the right person, with sound knowledge and good judgement.

mcq.questionText: A person who carries out da'wah is called a:
mcq.explanation: A da'i (plural du'at) is one who invites or calls people to Islam and to good conduct.

mcq.questionText: Which verse of the Qur'an establishes that there is no compulsion in religion?
mcq.explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:256 declares 'There is no compulsion in religion', showing that da'wah must be by invitation and persuasion, never by force.

mcq.questionText: According to Islamic teaching, the most effective form of da'wah is:
mcq.explanation: The best da'wah is good conduct. People are most strongly attracted to Islam when they see the honesty, kindness and good manners of a Muslim.

mcq.questionText: Where did the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) begin his da'wah in its earliest, secret stage?

options.text: Among the rulers of Persia and Rome
Among his close family and trusted friends

mcq.explanation: Da'wah began secretly among the Prophet's close family and trusted friends, such as Khadijah, Abu Bakr, Ali and Zaid, before it was made public.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a key quality of a good da'i?
mcq.explanation: A good da'i must have knowledge, patience (sabr), sincerity (ikhlas), gentleness and must lead by example.

mcq.questionText: The phrase 'maw'izah hasanah' in da'wah means:
mcq.explanation: Maw'izah hasanah means good or beautiful preaching: kind advice and exhortation that softens hearts and encourages people towards good.

mcq.questionText: What should be the intention (niyyah) behind doing da'wah?

options.text: To seek the pleasure of Allah

mcq.explanation: Da'wah must be done with sincerity (ikhlas), seeking only the pleasure of Allah, not for personal fame, wealth or power.

mcq.questionText: When arguing or debating with others in da'wah, the Qur'an instructs the believer to:

options.text: Argue in the way that is best (kindest and most respectful)
Refuse to listen to any objection

mcq.explanation: Surah An-Nahl 16:125 commands that one should argue with people in the best and most gracious manner, with respect and good reasoning.

mcq.questionText: Which of these is a common challenge faced by those doing da'wah?

options.text: Having too many followers at once

mcq.explanation: Du'at often face rejection, mockery, opposition and sometimes persecution, just as the Prophet (PBUH) did in Makkah. These are overcome with patience and trust in Allah.

mcq.questionText: In the modern world, an effective additional means of da'wah is:

options.text: Media such as television, radio and the internet
Forcing schools to teach only Islam

mcq.explanation: Modern media such as television, radio, books, social media and the internet allow the message of Islam to reach large audiences peacefully and quickly.

mcq.questionText: Why is da'wah considered an obligation upon the Muslim community?

options.text: Because it brings money to the mosque
Because Allah commands believers to invite to good and forbid evil
Because it is a tradition only of Arab people
Because it is optional and rarely needed

mcq.explanation: Allah commands the believers to call to good and forbid evil (Surah Aal-Imran 3:104), making da'wah a collective duty of the Muslim ummah.

mcq.questionText: Which behaviour of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) made his da'wah successful even before he openly preached?
mcq.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) was known as Al-Amin (the trustworthy) even before prophethood. His honesty and good character were themselves a powerful form of da'wah.

fib.questionText: The Arabic word da'wah literally means to call or _____ people.
fib.explanation: Da'wah means calling or inviting people to Islam and to all that is good.

fib.questionText: A person who calls people to Islam is known as a _____.
fib.explanation: The one who carries out da'wah is called a da'i.

fib.questionText: The three methods of da'wah are found in Surah An-Nahl, chapter 16, verse _____.
fib.explanation: Surah An-Nahl 16:125 outlines wisdom, good preaching and arguing in the best manner.

fib.questionText: The Arabic term for wisdom in da'wah is _____.
fib.explanation: Hikmah (wisdom) is the first method mentioned for inviting people to the way of Allah.

fib.questionText: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:256 states that there is no _____ in religion.
fib.explanation: There is no compulsion in religion, so da'wah is by invitation and persuasion, never by force.

fib.questionText: The best and most powerful form of da'wah is good _____ and good conduct.
fib.explanation: Good example and good character attract people to Islam more than words alone.

fib.questionText: The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was known among his people as Al-Amin, meaning the _____ one.
fib.explanation: Al-Amin means the trustworthy, a reputation that supported the Prophet's da'wah.

fib.questionText: Sincerity in doing da'wah for the sake of Allah is expressed in Arabic by the word _____.
fib.explanation: Ikhlas (sincerity) means doing da'wah purely to seek the pleasure of Allah.

fib.questionText: The Arabic word for patience, an essential quality of a da'i, is _____.
fib.explanation: Sabr (patience) is needed because du'at often face rejection and opposition.

fib.questionText: In the modern world, da'wah can reach many people through _____ such as the internet and television.
fib.explanation: Modern media (internet, television, radio, books) help spread the message of Islam widely and peacefully.

tf.questionText: Da'wah means inviting and calling people to Islam and to good.
tf.explanation: This is the correct meaning of da'wah: calling people to Islam and to all that is good.

tf.questionText: Islam permits the use of force to make people accept the religion.
tf.explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:256 says there is no compulsion in religion; da'wah is by invitation, not force.

tf.questionText: Wisdom (hikmah), good preaching (maw'izah hasanah) and arguing in the best manner are methods of da'wah from Surah An-Nahl 16:125.
tf.explanation: These three methods are clearly mentioned in Surah An-Nahl 16:125.

tf.questionText: A da'i should be harsh and insulting towards those who disagree.
tf.explanation: A da'i should be gentle, patient and respectful, arguing in the best manner.

tf.questionText: Good character and good conduct are considered the most effective form of da'wah.
tf.explanation: The best da'wah is good behaviour, which attracts people to Islam.

tf.questionText: Da'wah is only the duty of scholars and imams, not ordinary Muslims.
tf.explanation: Every Muslim shares in the duty of inviting to good according to their ability and knowledge.

tf.questionText: The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) began his da'wah secretly among his close family and friends.
tf.explanation: Da'wah started secretly with people like Khadijah, Abu Bakr and Ali before becoming public.

tf.questionText: Sincerity (ikhlas) means doing da'wah to gain fame and wealth.
tf.explanation: Ikhlas means doing da'wah purely for the sake of Allah, not for fame or wealth.

tf.questionText: Patience is needed in da'wah because callers often face rejection and opposition.
tf.explanation: Du'at face challenges such as ridicule and rejection, which require patience (sabr).

tf.questionText: Modern media such as the internet and television cannot be used for da'wah.
tf.explanation: Modern media are valuable tools for spreading the message of Islam peacefully and widely.

summary.questionText: Define the term da'wah as understood in Islam.
summary.correctAnswer: Da'wah means inviting, calling or summoning people to accept Islam and to do good while avoiding evil.
summary.explanation: Da'wah is the act of calling people to the way of Allah and to all that is good.

summary.questionText: Name the three methods of da'wah mentioned in Surah An-Nahl 16:125.
summary.correctAnswer: Wisdom (hikmah), good preaching (maw'izah hasanah) and arguing in the best manner.
summary.explanation: These three methods guide how a Muslim should invite others to Islam.

summary.questionText: Why is the principle 'there is no compulsion in religion' important for da'wah?
summary.correctAnswer: It shows that people must accept Islam freely through invitation and persuasion, not by force.
summary.explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:256 makes clear that faith must be a free choice.

summary.questionText: List three important qualities of a good da'i.
summary.correctAnswer: Knowledge, patience and sincerity (also gentleness and leading by good example).
summary.explanation: A good caller must combine sound knowledge with patience, sincerity and good conduct.

summary.questionText: Why is good character described as the best form of da'wah?
summary.correctAnswer: Because people are most attracted to Islam when they see honesty, kindness and good manners in Muslims.
summary.explanation: Good conduct demonstrates Islam in practice and softens the hearts of others.

summary.questionText: How did the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) spread Islam peacefully in its early stage?
summary.correctAnswer: He began secretly with close family and friends, then preached openly with patience, good example and gentle invitation.
summary.explanation: His da'wah moved from a secret stage to an open stage, always relying on good character and patience.

summary.questionText: State two manners or etiquette that should be observed in da'wah.
summary.correctAnswer: Showing respect and tolerance towards others, and never using compulsion or insult.
summary.explanation: Good manners such as respect, tolerance and gentleness are essential to da'wah.

summary.questionText: Mention two challenges commonly faced in da'wah.
summary.correctAnswer: Rejection or ridicule from people, and opposition or persecution.
summary.explanation: Du'at often face mockery and opposition, just as the early Muslims did in Makkah.

summary.questionText: How can the challenges of da'wah be overcome?
summary.correctAnswer: Through patience (sabr), trust in Allah, sincerity, sound knowledge and continued good conduct.
summary.explanation: Patience and reliance on Allah help a da'i continue despite difficulties.

summary.questionText: Give two ways da'wah can be carried out in the modern world.
summary.correctAnswer: Through media such as television, radio and the internet, and through Islamic books, lectures and social media.
summary.explanation: Modern technology allows the message of Islam to reach a wide audience peacefully.

hoq.questionText: A young Muslim wants to invite a non-Muslim classmate to learn about Islam. Which approach best reflects the Qur'anic method of da'wah?

options.text: Mocking the classmate's beliefs until they feel ashamed
Speaking with wisdom and kindness, and showing good character
Refusing to answer any of their questions

hoq.explanation: Surah An-Nahl 16:125 calls for wisdom, good preaching and the best manner. Combined with good character, this is the correct Qur'anic approach to da'wah.

hoq.questionText: A da'i is repeatedly mocked and rejected when inviting people to Islam. Based on the example of the Prophet (PBUH), what is the most appropriate response?

options.text: Abandon da'wah completely and give up
Remain patient, continue with good conduct, and trust in Allah
Force the people to accept Islam

hoq.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) faced ridicule and persecution in Makkah yet remained patient, continued his good conduct and trusted in Allah. Patience (sabr) is the model response.

hoq.questionText: Two Muslim youths discuss using social media for da'wah. Which use best fulfils the purpose and etiquette of da'wah?

options.text: Posting respectful, accurate content that invites people to good with wisdom
Spreading false information to win arguments
Insulting people of other faiths online
Demanding that followers convert immediately or be blocked

hoq.explanation: Modern media is a valid means of da'wah when used with accuracy, respect and wisdom, in keeping with the etiquette of inviting people to good without compulsion.
